newsitem.title: USA: Ford refuses comment on plant closing report.
newsitem.headline: Ford refuses comment on plant closing report.

text.p: A Ford Motor Co spokesman refused to make any comments Thursday on a Wall Street Journal story that the automaker is considering closing some plants, calling the report speculation.
"This is pure speculation," said company spokesman Timothy Chappell.
Chappell would not comment on the report's accuracy or say if Ford were considering the move, adding, "That's all I can tell you."

The story said no decisions have been made and it could take two or three years before any facilities are shuttered. One plant said to be vulnerable is the assembly facility in Lorain, Ohio, which makes the slow-selling Thunderbird and Cougar coupes, as well as Ford's full-size vans.
The plant, which occupies 4.1 million square feet, employs about 3,600 hourly workers and another 300 salaried workers.

With several new models being introduced over the next years, Ford is looking for ways to streamline its manufacturing facilities, the story said. Ford is also reported to be concerned about an industry sales downturn.

Ford's new three-year contract with the United Auto Worker union guarantees it will keep 95 percent of its current 105,000 hourly workers. However, the contract contains several exceptions to that rule, one of which involves a severe drop-off in sales.
